Want to know the crazy thing with old F1 cars? You steer with the wheel, throttle, and brake. All 3. It makes sense once you get it, but until then it's maddening.

If you go into the corner hot and brake late, the car gets unsettled. If you go in slow and leave hot, the car gets unsettled. If you go in at the right speed, you probably have significant understeer. So your only option is one of the first two, using the gas and/or brake to control your turn. Very often you find yourself using all three.

I was driving from somewhere, south to north.  Just cruising along on the highway, when all of a sudden the vehicle stalled.  Don't panic, did I just mess up my fuel?  Nope, I have good fuel.  Did I bork up my checklist and forget something?  Nope, the vehicle is configured as it should be.  I literally have no idea why the engine shut down.  I configure it to coast, get the backup power on (it starts, good sign).  Still don't panic, work towards restarting the engine.  Still don't panic, the engine starts and goes.  Don't panic, just drove over the state border, and I know up ahead is a local service station, so I can pull over very safely there.  Still not panicking, pull up the maps for the route and accept a detour for the stop. Praying the whole time, I make the turn on the dots.  The engine didn't shut down again.  I sat there for an hour going over my procedures, trying to figure it out.  I could never figure it out, except a bug in the vehicle. Needless to say, always keep a level head.  From up on the highway down to the ground, I always had a couple plans in case the vehicle went out.  The backup power was still running just in case it was needed, but even as far down as the final approach I was visually scanning for fields for a non-field stop. edit - Actually, another person reminded me of another bad one I had.  Final to a major destination one day, the weather in the area had been bad, but had improved by the time I landed.  Unfortunately, I was using default weather and apparently one of the stations didn't get the memo.  I was about 1000 feet up when the 15 knot headwind turned into a 20 knot tailwind, and I plummet 900 feet towards the houses under the approach path. Only 900 feet, because I was somehow able to halt the stall just above treetop level.  Needless to say I just walled the throttles and went around.  My hands didn't stop shaking for another hour or so, and I had trouble sleeping that night due to the adrenaline.
Hence my flair, the first thing I decided to screw around with on the vehicle.

There I was, a specific age and washed up.  When my right knee blew up on my for the second time on the ice in a city, so went my hockey career.  It wasn't much of a career anyways, only about a hundred-odd games in the top league (in five different cities, that has to be some kind of record).  I wound up where I had started after college hockey, in a major west coast city.  I had made a couple friends in the city, and had been set up to be the hockey advisor for the comedy film "The Terrible One."  Yes, that's a zero in the title.  I'm pretty sure I was only hired so that they could point at someone and say that they had a real hockey player advise on the scenes.  Oh well, I got paid better than I ever did in the minor leagues, and I can honestly say I'm probably the only person outside a specific province to get to see a full mascot line brawl. Jesus tapdancing Christ that hurts to even think about.  I need to ice my knee. I met my partner three months ago.  We were the results of a conspiracy of matchmakers who realized we both shared the same alma mater, THE (snicker) University of Michigan.  She's a specific age, and an actress.  Her most famous role had been about 5 years prior when she played one of about a dozen patients to die in a disaster on a medical drama.  Most of her roles had been independent films, or glorified extras in poorly performing studio films.  What made me fall in love almost instantly was her honesty.  She actually saw me play my senior year.  She even confessed to heckling me while drunk.  I remember the game against a rival; no goals, two terrible turnovers, and getting my ass kicked in a fight as the final horn sounded on a 6-0 drubbing at the hands of our in-state rival.  She was willing to give me shit about that game, and damn if I didn't love her for that. We had been dating for three months, when she invited me to go with her to her movie premier.  It was an independent drama about a woman trying to escape a cult, and she was one of the fellow cult members of the main female star.  When anyone thinks of what a movie premier is about, they think of the Chinese Theater.  For comparison, this one was held in a different city.  I didn't care, I got to spend a nice weekend out of town with her, we got to be by ourselves for the drive there and back, and I personally thought she did a great job in her role (she's her own worst critic, she had to walk out halfway through the movie).  We were in love before, but as she tells the story, me holding her in the lobby of the old theater in that city while she sobbed was when she knew that she truly loved me, and I loved her. So when the awards season came, and she was nominated for fucking everything, our lives changed.  Then three months after her movie was released, when she won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress in what was called the biggest surprise win in Academy Award history, I was suddenly dating a celebrity. That was five years ago.  I proposed a week after she won (I had the damn ring on me at the Oscars, I was going to propose as a consolation), and were married a little over a year after that.  After a few years of her supporting me while I scouted the world for the team, now I'm trying to pull my own weight.  Next year I'll be one of the assistant coaches for the minor league team.  It's a small step, and we've made a pact to be together as much as possible, given our schedules.  There's been some ups and downs, and her career damn near hit a speed bump the film afterwards.  Now that she's had a couple other major roles, one of which grossed just north of $500 million, she's reached a good place in her career.  Which is great for us, because everything's going to change in 6 months when our baby is born.

Not cool.  No reason to kick someone for having a bad landing. The best thing you could do on MP to start is to find a server that has a decent mission and low population.  Fly around, get some situational awareness, hell even go up with just heaters and ECM pods.  Draw the SAM sites out of hiding.  Learn to avoid and defend against launches, because if you’re going to hunt SAMs, you’re going to get shot at.  Once you’re comfortable getting shot at, load up the SEAD pod and a couple 25’s, and learn to do the close-in killing.  ZSU-23’s are best left to cluster bombs or vikhrs, or even a two person team to draw it out if hiding.  Once you get the shorter range antiradiation missiles, the 58’s are piece of cake.  Start small, get bigger.  Do it in steps, and only move on once you’re comfortable.  I’m at the point now that I know what’s firing on me by instinct (they’re doing what I’d do if I were them!), and I don’t usually get too concerned unless I’m at max weight. If you’re on during evening hours, jump on a popular server, and there’s a good chance I’ll be on.  If not during those hours, that server is still great.  there’s a really good group who’s helpful, and know SEAD really well.  Bonus for the fact that it’s a really welcoming group of pilots as well.

When I was a young teen, my parents drove me to the nearest store to rent a game for a popular console.  What followed is one of my greatest misses, in a way. Now, there were three people who worked at this store; the owner, who was probably in his 20's-30's and was a gamer even back in the early-mid 90's when this happened.  The second was a fat guy with a goatee, like the Chicken Man in Toy Story 2.  The third, however, was a younger woman, probably in the 18-26 age range. She was at the desk that day, and her and I were the only people in the store.  Nothing was amiss, no weirdness going on in the store.  I went back to the game section, and started searching for whatever game I wanted to rent that night.  After about 15 minutes, I picked the game, got my money out and went to the front desk where holy shit the lady's not wearing a shirt.  She had stripped down to her bra. Okay, I'll power through this.  I'm not sure what she's doing, because it was the middle of the summer, and it was probably 90 out that day.  She's probably just hot, yeah, that's it. Then she asks the question that I still wonder what the fuck she was trying to do. "Have you ever seen a grown woman like me?" Uhhh I paid and left.  Looking back on the situation, the whole thing was fucking weird. Right around that time, coincidentally, I started paying more attention to the girls at my school. Also, I never saw the lady again.  I tried to slyly bring it up with the owner later on, and he gave me the look of a guy who knew why I was asking.  He changed the subject to the games I was renting. When I mentioned the next school year that I almost scored with someone possibly twice my age, nobody believed me.
